question: Whether a single taxpayer who qualifies both for case L (raised a child alone five years) and case P (CMI invalidite, 80 %) gets two half-parts, and which quotient-familial cap applies.
facts: Single (celibataire, divorced or widowed; not specified) taxpayer without dependants, already benefiting from the case L half-part; holder of the CMI 'invalidite' (80 % incapacity) from 26 June 2017, granted retroactively by a judgment of 12 January 2021. Years 2017 to 2020 in dispute; incomes not stated.
assumptions: situation not stated (celibataire, divorcee or veuve): 0AC used; it does not change the number of parts
both case L and case P boxes set, as the taxpayer qualifies for both
income year 2020 chosen among the years in dispute (2017-2020); the holding is identical for each

NBPT.note: ¶ 5: 'qui bénéficie d'un quotient familial de 1,5'; ¶ 4: the two half-parts of art. 195, 1 do not cumulate

holding: The half-parts of art. 195, 1 do not cumulate (1.5 parts), but the tax must be computed with the quotient-familial cap of case d bis rather than the lower cap of case a; partial discharge.
quote: les deux demi-parts des dispositions du 1 de l'article 195 du code général des impôts ne peuvent se cumuler
notes: Art. 1 orders the tax computed 'selon les règles d'application du quotient familial plafonné prévu pour ... d bis ... et non du a': when L and P both apply, the more favourable treatment (general cap per half-part plus the art. 197 complementary reduction for d bis) replaces the specific case L cap (938 euros quoted). A program given 0AL=1 and 0AP=1 should give 1.5 parts and apply the P cap, not the L cap; incomes are not stated, so the cap effect cannot be scored here.

question: Whether a mother of two children in alternate residence who lives with a partner (concubinage) gets the parent-isole majoration (case T), and whether her partner's child counts.
facts: Unmarried mother of two children born 2014 and 2016 from a previous union, in alternate residence (charge equally shared). Living with a partner on 1 January 2021; the partner's own child also stays one week in two. Declared a taxable income of 28 491 euros and 1.5 parts for 2021.
assumptions: situation not stated beyond a previous union and concubinage: 0AC used (cohabiting partners are taxed separately); parts unaffected
taxpayer alt_boxes combine both claims (case T, and the partner's child as a third alternate-residence child); that child's birth year is not stated and omitted

NBPT.note: ¶ 1: declared 1,5 part; ¶ 4 rejects case T, ¶ 6 rejects the third child

holding: A taxpayer living with a partner does not live alone, even if the partner does not support her children, so no case T majoration; the partner's child was not taken into her household. Request rejected.
quote: Dans ces conditions, et alors même que son concubin n'aurait pas la charge de ses deux enfants, elle ne peut être regardée comme vivant seule.
notes: The declared taxable income of 28 491 euros (2021) is stated but its composition is not, so no tax figure is scored.

question: Number of parts and deductible alimony of a separated husband taxed separately (art. 6, 4), whose adult daughter is attached to his household while the two minor children live with their mother.
facts: Spouses separated in 2019 (non-conciliation order of 17 June 2019) and taxed separately under art. 6, 4. The husband keeps the marital home; the eldest (adult) daughter chose to be attached to his household; the two minor children reside with their mother. Under the order he owes 1 000 euros per month to his wife and 500 euros per month per child. He declared 500 euros per child for three children (18 000 euros); the deduction was allowed only for the two minor children (12 000 euros), the adult daughter being attached. Taxed on his own incomes: non-commercial profits of 154418 euros and property income of 10222 euros.
assumptions: married but taxed separately under art. 6, 4: coded 0AD (separated)
case T (0BT) assumed: the 2 parts retained are reached only as 1 + 0.5 (attached adult child) + 0.5 (parent isole); the decision attributes them to the attachment and does not mention case T

6GU = 24 000: the court records a deduction of alimony of 24 000 euros, 12 000 of it for the two minor children (500 x 2 x 12); the other 12 000 is taken to be the 1 000 euros per month owed to the wife
the non-commercial profits and property income are stated but not their regime (approved-association membership, micro or real property regime), so no income boxes are given

NBPT.note: ¶ 19: 'avec deux parts de quotient familial compte tenu du rattachement de sa fille majeure'

PA_DED.note: ¶ 19: 'déduction des pensions alimentaires versées pour 24 000 euros'; ¶ 17: 12 000 of it for the two minor children

holding: Separate taxation was rightly applied; the taxpayer cannot, for the same child, both deduct alimony and gain a part through attachment, so the adult daughter's alimony is not deductible and 3 parts are refused. Requests rejected.
quote: Une imposition supplémentaire a été établie [...] avec deux parts de quotient familial compte tenu du rattachement de sa fille majeure à son foyer fiscal
notes: The 'imposition nette' of 25 218 euros in the decision includes social levies and penalties, after deducting half of joint advance payments, so it is not an income-tax figure. The taxpayer claimed 3 parts (all three children) together with the alimony deduction.

question: Whether an unmarried father separated in 2020 from the mother of a child born on 17 January 2020 is entitled to a 0.25-part majoration for a child whose charge was equally shared.
facts: Unmarried father, taxed separately from the child's mother; daughter born 17 January 2020; de facto separation during 2020; family charges assessed at 31 December 2020 (art. 196 bis). The court finds the child's maintenance was shared equally in 2020. No case T claimed.
assumptions: situation coded 0AC (unmarried); a past PACS is not mentioned and would not change the parts
case T not set: not claimed, and the court fixes 1.25 parts

NBPT.note: Art. 1 of the judgment

holding: The presumption that the child is at the charge of the parent with whom it mainly lives is rebutted by evidence of equally shared costs; the father gets 0.25 part and the tax is reduced accordingly.
quote: Le quotient familial [...] pour le calcul de l'impôt sur le revenu au titre de l'année 2020 est fixé à 1,25 parts.

question: Whether a single taxpayer already entitled to the case L half-part gets a second half-part as holder of a disability card since March 2019.
facts: Single (situation not specified) taxpayer without dependants, entitled to the art. 195, 1 a half-part, holder of a disability card since March 2019. Received in 2019 back pay of 21 393,72 euros gross under a labour-court judgment; income tax 2019 of 3 014 euros.
assumptions: situation not stated: 0AC used; parts unaffected
income year 2019 is outside the 2020-2025 batch range, but the number of parts is year-independent
her other incomes are not stated (only the gross back pay), so no income boxes

NBPT.note: ¶ 3: art. 195 only raises the quotient from 1 to 1,5 whatever the number of cases met

holding: Art. 195, 1 only takes the quotient from 1 to 1.5 and never grants several half-parts to a taxpayer meeting several of its cases; the back pay is taxable in the year received. Request rejected.
quote: ne prévoit nullement l'octroi de plusieurs demi-parts supplémentaires pour un contribuable répondant à plusieurs de ces hypothèses
notes: Same non-cumulation rule as TA Bordeaux 16 March 2023 n° 2101566 (b1_2101566_20230316_2020), which adds that the d bis cap then applies. The 3 014 euros tax cannot be scored: incomes other than the gross back pay are not stated.

question: Whether a married man taxed alone as divorced/separated (case L, 1.5 parts) can count his wife's part or deduct the sums he pays her as contribution to the marriage costs.
facts: Taxpayer imposed for 2020 as divorced/separated with 1.5 parts under case L (raised a child alone at least five years, child not attached); income tax 553 euros for 2020 (1 151 euros for 2019 as celibataire, 1.5 parts). assumptions: situation 0AD (divorced/separated) as on the 2020 assessment quoted by the court

NBPT.note: ¶ 1: imposed for 2020 'avec un quotient familial de 1,5 part en tant que divorcé/séparé ayant élevé seul ... un enfant'

holding: The payments to the wife are not shown to match the spouses' respective means nor to have been used for household needs; no deduction and no change to the quotient. Request rejected.

question: Whether the default withholding rate applied to back pay was refundable; the court sets out the full 2021 tax computation.
facts: Retired single-person household with 1.5 parts; revenu brut global 2021 of 24 935 euros including back pay from a former employer; over-65 allowance applied; taxable income 23 693 euros.
assumptions: Income composition (pensions vs. back pay) not stated: only the revenu brut global (24 935) is given, so no income boxes are encoded; score from RBG.
Marital status and reason for the extra half-part not stated: encoded as single + case L as a placeholder; any status/case giving 1.5 parts works (QF advantage 562 euros is below every cap).

Single-person decote parameters (790 / 45.25 %) used by the court.

A157BIS.note: para 6: difference between RBG 24 935 and taxable income 23 693

NBPT.note: para 6

question: Whether a stock-option acquisition gain should be taxed under the quotient system (art. 163-0 A).
facts: Single-member household (1 part); revenu net global 2020 excluding the gain 168 870 euros; acquisition gain on stock options 1 426 887 euros.
assumptions: Only the revenu net global excluding the gain (168 870) is stated; it is given in court_figures, not as income boxes.
Household status not stated beyond 'seul membre de son foyer fiscal': encoded as single (1 part).
0XX used for the exceptional income under the quotient; the comparison is quotient vs. inclusion of the same net amount in ordinary income.

holding: Request rejected: claims to validate the amended return are inadmissible and, in any event, the quotient would not change the tax since the ordinary income is already in the top 45 % bracket.
quote: son revenu net taxable hors quotient était supérieur à la plus haute fraction marginale d’imposition définie à l’article 197
notes: Correct for 1 part: Q/4 taxed at 45 %, times 4 = 45 % of Q, identical to no quotient. Court quotes the 2020-income scale (10 084 / 25 710 / 73 516 / 158 122).

question: Whether the withholding rate should take account of the household's recurring tax reductions and credits.

FCPI and ESUS reductions (3 828 and 1 250 euros, stated) not encoded: subscription amounts not stated.
Union dues assigned to declarant 1 (7AC); who paid them is not stated.
Ages not stated; the home-employment cap is not binding (8 507 < 12 000).

CRED_TOTAL.note: para 12: combined credit for home employment (50 % of 8 507) and union dues (66 % of 320)

holding: Rejected: the withholding rate legitimately excludes reductions and credits, which are refunded through the January advance and the final assessment.
quote: Le crédit d'impôt en résultant s'est alors élevé à la somme de 4 465 euros.
notes: Also stated: January 2022 advance 3 811 (60 % of recurring reductions/credits), refund 9 543; FCPI 3 828, ESUS 1 250; 2022 tax 17 063 with 17 362 withheld at 16.8 %. Total niches incl. FCPI/ESUS about 9 332, below the 10 000 cap.

question: Whether military pension arrears later repaid could be removed from 2021 income; the tax after correction of the number of parts is stated.
facts: Divorced taxpayer with two dependent children; 2021 salaries 37 144 euros and pension 16 323 euros (of which 15 507.40 repaid in 2022).

Salaries and pension taken as net taxable amounts (1AJ / 1AS).

IR_NET.note: paras 1 and 3: tax after correction of the quotient familial

TAX_DELTA.note: 5 617 initial tax minus 3 453 after correcting the number of parts (para 1)

question: Whether an alleged impatriation bonus could be excluded from the worldwide income used for the effective rate.
facts: Married couple leaving France in August 2020; French-taxed salaries 45 960 euros (husband: 74 377 paid minus 28 417 declared exempt) and 10 360 euros (wife); 10 % deduction gives RBG 50 688 euros.

holding: Rejected: the payment was not an impatriation bonus; the administration could substitute grounds and include it in worldwide income for the effective rate (art. 197 C).

notes: Tax assessed 3 564 euros (effective-rate method with foreign income), not reproducible from the stated facts.

question: Whether, for the CEHR smoothing rule, the reference incomes of prior years were those of the parents' household to which the taxpayers were attached.
facts: Three siblings, each a separate single household in 2020, each declaring a net capital gain of 1 059 216 euros; they had been attached to their parents' household in 2018.
assumptions: Each taxpayer encoded as single with no other income; RFR assumed equal to the declared net gain.

Prior-year RFRs (parents' household) not stated, so the smoothed CEHR is not scorable.

CEHR.note: TA para 1: CEHR before smoothing; 3 % x 250 000 + 4 % x (1 059 216 - 500 000) = 29 868.64

holding: Appeal dismissed: the smoothing compares with the average RFR of the household to which the taxpayers belonged in prior years (the parents'); the partial degrevement of 7 675 granted by the administration stands.
quote: c'est à bon droit que l'administration a pris en compte, dans le calcul du dispositif du quotient, l'ensemble des revenus du foyer fiscal
notes: Smoothed CEHR = 29 869 - 7 675 = 22 194 per taxpayer (as granted), but prior RFRs are not stated. Duplicates: TA Bordeaux 2023-05-17 n° 2106629, 2106631, 2106632.

question: Whether a compensatory allowance paid as 450 000 euros of capital plus monthly instalments over eight years was deductible or gave the art. 199 octodecies reduction.
facts: Divorce by mutual consent in February 2020; compensatory allowance of 613 200 euros payable as 50 000 + 400 000 within a month and 1 700 euros a month for eight years; the taxpayer deducted 467 000 euros as alimony.
assumptions: Only the capital part paid within 12 months (450 000) is encoded for the reduction; the reduction is capped at 25 % of 30 500 whatever the exact base.
Treatment of the monthly instalments paid in 2020 is not stated; not encoded.
Household and other incomes not stated; the tax is assumed to exceed the reduction (supplement of 238 132 euros).
reviewer: household and income not stated; a probe salary of 200 000 added so that the tax exceeds the reduction
holding: Rejected: the capital part is not deductible but gives the 25 % reduction capped at 30 500, i.e. 7 625 euros; the 2012 doctrine no longer applies after the 2020 QPC decision.
quote: l’administration fiscale a évalué, dans sa proposition de rectification, sans commettre d’erreur de droit, la réduction d’impôt à 7 625 euros
notes: The court treats the eight-year instalments as a rente making the allowance 'mixed', yet grants the reduction on the capital part, relying on the repeal of art. 199 octodecies II after Cons. const. 2019-824 QPC.

question: Whether gifts and volunteer expenses gave the 66 % donation reduction.
facts: Taxpayer claimed, after filing, gifts of 110 and 60 euros and 2 034 euros of volunteer expenses; the administration granted the reduction for the 60 euros gift during the proceedings.
assumptions: Household and income not stated; the delta assumes the tax exceeds the reduction and the 20 % limit is not binding.
Only the 60 euros gift (accepted) is encoded; the 2 034 euros expenses were rejected; the fate of the 110 euros subscription is not stated.
reviewer: household and income not stated; a probe salary of 50 000 (single) added to both versions so that the tax exceeds the reduction and the 20 % limit does not bind

TAX_DELTA.note: para 2: degrevement of 40 euros for the 60 euros gift

holding: Non-lieu for the 40 euros granted; the volunteer expenses were not shown to qualify, so the rest is rejected.
quote: a procédé au dégrèvement d’une somme de 40 € correspondant à la réduction d’impôt relative au don de 60 €
notes: 66 % x 60 = 39.60, rounded to 40.

question: Whether a secondary-school grant was rightly refused on the household's resources (the tax notice states the household's parts).

NBPT.note: tax notice 2021 on 2020 income, cited by the court

quote: fait état d'un revenu fiscal de référence de 3 343 euros pour un nombre de parts fixés à 4 et 3 enfants à charge
notes: Dispute concerns a school grant, not income tax; the parts figure comes from the income-tax notice.

question: Whether a secondary-school grant was rightly refused on the household's resources (the tax notice states six parts).

notes: Dispute concerns a school grant; the parts figure comes from the income-tax notice.

question: Whether the taxpayer, a single person, is entitled to the extra half-part for holders of the veteran card over 74 (art. 195, 1 f).
facts: Single taxpayer without dependants, entitled to the half-part of art. 195, 1 f (veteran). The administration recomputed the 2018 tax with 1.5 parts instead of 1 part after a claim; the taxpayer then sought a refund on another ground.

declarant over 74 and holder of the veteran card or pension (implied by the grant under art. 195, 1 f)

reviewer: the half-part of art. 195, 1 f requires the declarant to be over 74; birth year not stated, 1940 entered (first run used the runner's default 1980 and gave 1 part: a mapping error, not a program error)

NBPT.note: para 3: tax recomputed with "un quotient familial d'une part et demi"; para 4: not contested

notes: Para 2-3 also give "impôt calculé" 3 283 euros with 1 part and 2 146 euros with 1.5 parts (before CIMR 3 254 / 2 127, home-employment credit 71, advance 299), but the income is not stated, so only the parts are scorable.

notes: Years 2013-2015; only 2015 is in scope. Uses the widower-with-child rule of art. 194 (2.5 parts).

question: Whether an infirm adult son of a married couple counts as a dependant (art. 196, 1°) and whether a further half-part for a disability card applies.

facts: Married couple; the husband was 77 in 2013 and says he is a veteran and disabled, his wife also disabled. Taxed on 2.5 parts for 2015 as declared; 3 parts admitted for 2016-2017.

question: Whether a separated mother had exclusive charge of her two children (2 parts) or alternate residence (1.5 parts).

holding: She did not show that the father failed to apply the alternate residence, so 1.5 parts were kept.
quote: alors que l'administration a retenu 1,5 part de quotient familial en considération de la garde alternée fixée pour la garde de ses deux enfants

question: Whether an unmarried father, whose two minor daughters were also declared by their mother, is entitled to half-parts or quarter-parts for them.
facts: Unmarried father; the mother of his two minor daughters declared them, lives in another town where they go to school; he claimed he lived with them.
assumptions: no other dependant

NBPT.note: quotient section: neither the two half-parts nor 0.25 part per child granted

holding: He did not prove he lived with the mother and the children; no increase of the quotient, not even the 0.25 part per child for shared charge. Partial relief on another point (requalification of sums as salaries).
quote: n'est pas fondé à soutenir qu'il était en droit de bénéficier d'une demi-part de quotient-familial à raison de la charge partagée de ses enfants
notes: Before the tribunal he claimed 2 parts (two half-parts); on appeal 0.25 per daughter. Years 2014-2015; 2015 used.

question: Whether a taxpayer married abroad in August 2016 could be taxed jointly with two parts for 2016.
facts: Taxpayer married abroad on 15 Aug 2016; the marriage was transcribed in the French civil register only on 8 April 2021. Taxed on one part.
assumptions: no dependants (none mentioned)

NBPT.note: para 3: no joint taxation before transcription

holding: Without transcription before the year in issue he could not be taxed jointly with his wife for 2016; one part kept.
quote: ne pouvait, dans ces conditions, être soumis à une imposition commune avec son épouse
notes: Unusual: the court makes joint taxation depend on the transcription of a foreign marriage, although it also cites the civil-code rule that such a marriage has civil effects between the spouses without transcription.

question: Number of parts of a married taxpayer whose spouse joined him in France on 3 Oct 2017 (separation of property, first part of the year).
facts: Taxpayer resident in France, married since 31 Oct 2016 under separation of property; spouse lived abroad until 2 Oct 2017. Period 1 Jan - 2 Oct 2017: separate taxation.
assumptions: separate taxation of a married person (art. 6, 4 a) entered as 0AD
no dependants

NBPT.note: art. 1 of the judgment: period 1 Jan - 2 Oct 2017 taxed on one part

holding: The tribunal split 2017: one part for 1 Jan - 2 Oct (spouses separated of property, not under the same roof), two parts for 3 Oct - 31 Dec (joint taxation).
quote: est établie sur la base d'un quotient familial d'une part
notes: Unusual: one income year split into two taxation periods (separate then joint) when the spouses came under the same roof; an annual program cannot model the split; see companion case _p2.

question: Number of parts for the period after the spouse came to live with the taxpayer (3 Oct - 31 Dec 2017).
facts: Married couple living under the same roof from 3 Oct 2017; the spouse had her centre of family interests in France and is treated as resident.
assumptions: no dependants

NBPT.note: art. 2 of the judgment: period 3 Oct - 31 Dec 2017 taxed jointly on two parts

holding: For 3 Oct - 31 Dec 2017 the couple is taxed jointly with two parts.
quote: est établie sur la base d'un quotient familial de deux parts, en tenant compte, pour la période en cause, de leurs revenus
notes: Companion of _p1: same decision, second taxation period of 2017.

question: Whether a divorced father had exclusive charge of his minor son in 2016 or only alternate residence.
facts: Divorced since April 2016; son born 1999 declared by the mother as in alternate residence for 2016; daughter born 1995 not attached. The father filed no return.
assumptions: the adult daughter (born 1995) is not attached

NBPT.note: para 3: the administration granted 0.25 part for 2016

holding: No proof of exclusive charge; the 0.25 part granted for alternate residence is kept.
quote: a dans sa propre déclaration de revenus porté son fils mineur en garde alternée et l'administration en a tiré les conséquences
notes: Taxpayer asked for one extra half-part for the son; case T not discussed.

question: Whether a divorced father could count his minor son in 2017 when the mother declared exclusive charge.
facts: Divorced father; the mother declared exclusive charge of their son (born 1999) on 1 Jan 2017 and obtained the half-part. He was taxed as divorced living alone without dependants.

NBPT.note: para 3: taxed as divorced without dependant in 2017

holding: No proof of exclusive charge; one part kept.
quote: a déclaré avoir la charge exclusive de leur fils et a à ce titre bénéficié d'un supplément de quotient familial

question: Whether an unmarried father had the custody of his son (1.5 parts) in 2018-2019.
facts: Unmarried parents separated since 2018; child born 2016 declared by the mother as at her charge; the father paid alimony and admitted his declaration was wrong.

NBPT.note: para 13: claim to 1.5 parts rejected

holding: The child is at the mother's charge; the claim to 1.5 parts is rejected.
quote: son quotient familial doit être porté à 1,5 part en raison de la garde de son fils en 2018 et 2019 doit être écarté
notes: Same holding for 2018; 2019 used.

question: Whether a separated father had his two minor children in alternate residence (1.5 parts) or only one part.
facts: Married man living separately from his wife, separate returns from 2017; the two minor children lived with their mother, not in alternate residence.
assumptions: separate taxation of separated spouses entered as 0AD

NBPT.note: para 1 and 5: quotient reduced from 1.5 to 1 part, claim rejected

holding: He did not show that he still lived with his family; the reduction to one part is upheld.
quote: ramener son quotient familial de 1,5 à 1 part dès lors que ses enfants vivaient avec leur mère et n'étaient pas en garde alternée
notes: The alimony deduction was also refused (no court decision, no proof of payment); amounts not stated.

question: Whether a father whose disabled daughter lives with her mother keeps the extra half-part he had in 2018.
facts: Unmarried father paying 200-400 euros a month to the mother of his disabled daughter, who lives with the mother.
assumptions: situation not stated; 0AC used
the daughter is not at his charge in 2019

NBPT.note: quotient was 1.5 in 2018 and 1 in 2019; no proof of entitlement

holding: He did not show any ground for a half-part in 2019; one part kept.
quote: qui était de 1,5 en 2018, est passé à 1 en 2019, sans que le requérant n'établisse qu'il pouvait bénéficier en 2019 d'une demi-part supplémentaire

question: Whether a taxpayer divorced on 22 Nov 2017 is taxed on one part for the whole year or pro rata married/divorced.
facts: Taxpayer divorced on 22 Nov 2017, no dependant, paying alimony of 400 euros a month.
assumptions: no dependants (as he declared)

NBPT.note: last paras: one part for 2017

holding: In the year of divorce each ex-spouse is taxed separately for the whole year on his own situation; one part.
quote: a été effectué sur la base d'un quotient familial de 1 part sur l'année 2017
notes: The taxpayer asked for a pro rata computation; art. 6, 6 and 196 bis apply instead.

question: Whether a father separating in 2015 can count his son whose residence was fixed with the mother.
facts: Spouses filed separate 2015 returns, each declaring their son; the non-conciliation order of 19 Jan 2016 fixed the son's residence with the mother, and he lived with her on 31 Dec 2015.
assumptions: separate taxation in the year of separation entered as 0AD

NBPT.note: para 10: one part for 2015

holding: The son lived with his mother on 31 Dec 2015; the father keeps one part. Partial relief on another point (CAVOM contributions).
quote: a été effectué sur la base d'un quotient familial d'une part pour les revenus de l'année 2015
notes: Child's situation assessed at 31 December in the year of separation (art. 196 bis).

question: Number of parts of an unmarried father living with the mother of their child, when neither proves exclusive charge.
facts: Unmarried cohabiting parents; daughter born 16 May 2014. The administration first allowed 1 part, then 1.25 parts after a claim; the father claimed 1.5.
assumptions: shared charge between cohabiting unmarried parents is entered as alternate residence (0CH) to obtain the 0.25 increase

NBPT.note: quotient section: 1.25 parts admitted, claim to a full half-part rejected

holding: Charge shared between cohabiting parents is split equally (0.25 each); the father did not prove exclusive charge.
quote: l'administration fiscale a admis de majorer le quotient familial à 1,25 parts qu'elle avait ramené à 1 part
notes: Unusual mapping: cohabiting (not separated) parents share the child half-part equally, the court applying the alternate-residence 0.25 by analogy. Same holding for 2017. Appeal from TA Dijon 2300836.

question: Whether a divorced father who counts his three children in alternate residence in his quotient can also deduct the alimony paid to their mother.
facts: Divorced since 2014; three minor children; he declared alternate residence (0.25 + 0.25 + 0.5 part) and deducted 25 200 euros a year of alimony paid to the mother.
assumptions: case T not claimed (only one extra part declared)
children minors in 2017

NBPT.note: paras 1 and 11: one extra part declared for three children in alternate residence, kept by the administration

holding: Counting the children in the quotient excludes deducting the alimony paid for them; the deduction is refused and the parts are kept.
quote: déduire la pension versée à son ex-épouse, ces deux dispositifs étant, en vertu des dispositions précitées, exclusifs l'un de l'autre
notes: Alimony of 25 200 euros (box 6GU) held not deductible because the children are counted in the quotient; not entered as a box to avoid double counting. Years 2015-2017; 2017 used.

question: Whether a disabled sister living under the taxpayer's roof but filing her own return can be counted as his dependant (art. 196 A bis).
facts: Single taxpayer; his sister, born 12 Jan 1970, holds the disability card (80%) and lives at his home, but filed her own returns for 2014 and 2015. Primitive taxation on one part; the tribunal had granted 2.5 parts.
assumptions: taxpayer single without other dependants (one part initially)

NBPT.note: paras 4 and 8: TA judgment annulled, one part restored

holding: A disabled person who files her own return forms her own tax household and cannot be a dependant under art. 196 A bis; the right-to-error rule does not apply.
quote: cette personne, alors même qu'elle vit sous le toit d'un autre contribuable, ne peut pas être considérée comme étant à charge de ce contribuable
notes: The tribunal (TA Versailles 2004727) had granted 2.5 parts; the alt_boxes 0CR alone may give 2 parts, the 2.5 claimed implies case T on top. Years 2014-2015; 2015 used.

question: Whether a divorced father had his minor son at his exclusive charge (half-part) or only 0.25 part.
facts: Divorced father; the mother declared their minor son as at her charge in 2015 and in alternate residence in 2016-2017; the administration applied a 0.25 increase.
assumptions: the son is treated as in alternate residence for 2015 as the administration did

NBPT.note: paras 4 and following: 0.25 increase instead of a half-part

holding: No proof of exclusive charge; the 0.25 majoration applied by the administration is kept.
quote: bénéficiait au titre de 2015 non d'une demi-part, mais d'une majoration de 0,25
notes: Same decision: alimony of 4 500 euros to an adult daughter, declared x1.25 (5 625) as paid under a pre-2006 judgment, held not deductible at all (paid under a 2011 private agreement, needs not proved). Relief of 7 591 euros on a Scellier-type reduction granted during the proceedings.

question: Whether a divorced father counted for 0.25 part for his son can also deduct the alimony paid to the mother.
facts: Divorced father; his son was counted for half of the child part (0.25) in his quotient; he asked to deduct the alimony paid to his ex-wife instead.
assumptions: no other dependant

NBPT.note: para 6: son counted for half of the child part

holding: Counting the child in the quotient, even for 0.25 part, excludes the alimony deduction; claim rejected.
quote: la prise en compte de l'enfant dans la détermination du quotient familial des contribuables interdit la déduction de la pension alimentaire
notes: Years 2016-2017; 2017 used. Alimony amounts not stated in the extract used.

question: Whether an unmarried father living with the mother can claim 0.25 part for their child whom the mother declared at her exclusive charge.
facts: Unmarried cohabiting parents until 2018; the mother declared their minor daughter at her exclusive charge in 2016 and received the half-part. The father claimed 1.25 parts.

NBPT.note: para 13: claim to count the child rejected

holding: He accepted the mother's declaration; no increase for him.
quote: Il déclare lui-même que son enfant a toujours été déclarée par sa mère et notamment en 2016 comme étant à sa charge exclusive ou principale
notes: Contrast with CAA Lyon 25LY00435, where the administration itself split the child part (0.25) between cohabiting parents.

question: Whether a single father whose daughter moved to alternate residence in August 2019 can have 1.25 parts while deducting alimony paid for her.
facts: Single father; daughter born 2008 in alternate residence since August 2019; he paid 4 360 euros of alimony for her in 2019, deducted from his income.

NBPT.note: para 5: the deducted alimony excludes counting the child

holding: The alimony for the daughter was deducted; he cannot also count her in his quotient. One part kept.
quote: une pension alimentaire au bénéfice de sa fille d'un montant de 4 360 euros, qui a été prise en compte par l'administration fiscale
notes: Situation on 1 Jan 2019 was not alternate residence; the court decides on the alimony/quotient exclusivity. Deducted alimony 4 360 euros (6GU) is an input, not entered.

question: Whether PACS partners who separated on 1 June 2016 are taxed jointly (2.5 parts) or separately.
facts: PACS partners with one child, separated since 1 June 2016 (new lease of the partner from 3 June 2016); the child stays with the mother. The administration taxed him alone on one part.
assumptions: separated partner taxed separately entered as 0AD
child at the mother's charge

NBPT.note: para 1 and 7: quotient reduced from 2.5 to one part, appeal rejected

holding: Separation from 1 June 2016 is established; separate taxation on one part.
quote: passant de 2,5 à une part, au motif qu'il vivait séparé de sa partenaire de pacte civil de solidarité (PACS) depuis le 1er juin 2016

question: Number of parts of a married man separated of property and living apart since 1984, and whether his infirm adult son can be attached.
facts: Married in 1962, separated of property, living apart since 1984: separate taxation. Granted the case L half-part for 2017 (1.5 parts). Son born 1964, infirm, in a care home, filed his own returns.
assumptions: separate taxation of spouses (art. 6, 4 a) entered as 0AD

NBPT.note: para 1: relief of 912 euros applying 1.5 parts (art. 195, 1); claim to 3 parts rejected

holding: Separate taxation upheld; the son, who filed his own returns, cannot be attached; 1.5 parts kept.
quote: a bénéficié d'un dégrèvement de 912 euros correspondant à l'application du quotient familial de 1,5 prévu au 1 de l'article 195
notes: Unusual: a married person living apart obtains case L as a person living alone. The 912 euros is the tax effect of 1 -> 1.5 parts but income is not stated. Year 2019 also in dispute (not used).

question: Whether a married couple can attach their adult student son after the filing deadline.
facts: Married couple with a minor daughter (2.5 parts declared); son born 1 Mar 1997, student, not declared as attached; attachment requested in Oct 2018 and Apr 2019.

NBPT.note: para 7: 2.5 parts applied, TA judgment annulled

holding: The option to attach an adult child must be made within the filing deadline; late request refused, 2.5 parts.
quote: refuser de prendre en compte cette demande de rattachement formulée dans le délai de réclamation mais après l'expiration du délai de déclaration
notes: Excess-of-power case on the refusal; the tribunal had annulled the refusal.

question: Number of parts for 2018 of spouses married under community who separated in July 2018 and divorced in 2021 with effects backdated to the separation.
facts: Married under community property; two children at charge on 1 Jan 2018; separated 17 July 2018; divorce agreement of 14 April 2021 backdates its effects to 17 July 2018. The administration kept 2 parts (parent isolé with one child) for 2018.
assumptions: two minor children fully dependent

NBPT.note: art. 1: 2018 tax computed with three parts

holding: The community was not dissolved on 1 Jan 2018 and the backdating has effect only between the spouses; three parts for 2018, taking the spouse's income into account for the rate.
quote: qui avait deux enfants à sa charge au 1er janvier 2018, est fondé à demander à bénéficier d'un quotient familial de trois parts
notes: Unusual: joint quotient kept for the year of separation by reference to the 1 January situation; the court says to include the spouse's income "le cas échéant" to fix the rate. 2017 already admitted at 3 parts.

question: Whether a separated mother of two children living with a companion keeps the parent isolé half-part (case T).
facts: Woman separated from her husband with their two children at her charge; the administration showed she lived with a companion. T half-part removed for 2014 and 2015.
assumptions: separately taxed married woman entered as 0AD
two minor children fully dependent

NBPT.note: case T removed, claim rejected

holding: She did not live alone on 1 January; the T half-part is refused.
quote: L'administration fiscale a remis en cause la demi-part correspondant à la situation de parent isolé dont a bénéficié

question: Whether a father of two daughters who shares an address with a companion keeps the parent isolé half-part (case T).
facts: Father with two daughters at his charge; he and his companion bought a home together in 2015 and both declared that address; common housing tax notice.
assumptions: two daughters (the decision speaks of "ses filles" and cites the two-children line of art. 194)
situation divorced or single not stated; 0AD used

NBPT.note: T half-part removed for 2017, claim rejected

holding: Cohabitation established; no T half-part for 2017.
quote: c'est à bon droit que l'administration a remis en cause le bénéfice d'une demi-part supplémentaire du quotient familial

question: Whether a single mother can attach her 22-year-old daughter who was not a student, and keep the parent isolé half-part.
facts: Single woman; daughter born 17 Sep 1992, not a student and unemployed in 2015, declared as attached; she declared herself parent isolé (2 parts).
assumptions: case L not claimed

NBPT.note: paras 10-11: attachment and T half-part refused

holding: Attachment of an adult child is reserved to students (under 25) here; refused, and the T half-part falls with it.
quote: s'est déclarée parent isolé, ce qui devait lui ouvrir droit à deux parts pour la prise en compte de son revenu imposable
notes: Same decision replaces real expenses by the 10% deduction (2 375 euros for 2015) but salaries are not stated.

question: Whether two adult student children can be attached on a late 2016 return.
facts: Taxpayer filed his 2016 return late (June 2020) declaring his two student children aged 20 and 21 as attached; undated letters from the children produced in the proceedings.
assumptions: situation single or divorced not stated; 0AC used (2 parts claimed with two attached children)

NBPT.note: para 4: attachment not established, claim to 2 parts rejected

holding: The children's request and acceptance within the time limit are not established; no attachment.
quote: aurait dû bénéficier de deux parts doit être écarté

question: Whether a married taxpayer is entitled to the invalidity half-part for years before his invalidity pension was granted.
facts: Married couple; the husband obtained a category-2 invalidity pension title on 2 Dec 2019. Taxed on 2 parts.
assumptions: no dependants (2 parts applied)

NBPT.note: invalidity half-part refused for the years in issue

holding: No invalidity pension of at least 40% or card in the years in issue; no extra half-part.
quote: c'est à bon droit que l'administration fiscale ne leur a pas attribué la demi-part supplémentaire
notes: Years 2013-2016 in issue; 2016 used.

question: Deductible amount of alimony paid to an adult daughter above the art. 196 B ceiling.
facts: Taxpayer paid 5 870 euros of alimony to his adult daughter in 2015.
assumptions: payer's own situation not stated; 0AC used (irrelevant to the deduction)
the daughter is not attached

PA_DED.note: para 3: the 5 870 euros exceed the art. 196 B ceiling for 2015; ceiling value as quoted in the decision

holding: Alimony to an adult child is deductible only up to the art. 196 B ceiling; claim rejected.
quote: est supérieur à l'abattement prévu par les dispositions précitées de l'article 196 B du code général des impôts au titre de l'année 2015
notes: The decision does not restate the amount allowed; PA_DED is the 2015 ceiling cited in the quoted art. 196 B (5 732 euros).

question: Whether a woman separated since 1991 qualifies for case L (raised a child alone for five years).
facts: Woman separated from her husband in 1991, living alone, no child at charge; her children were adults during the five years after the separation.

NBPT.note: case L refused

holding: Case L refused; partial relief of 150 euros for 2016 on another point.
quote: ne remplit pas les conditions prévues par les dispositions énoncées au point 5 pour bénéficier d'une demi-part supplémentaire de quotient familial

question: Whether a man divorced in 2005 qualifies for case L.
facts: Divorced since February 2005, no child at charge since the divorce, living alone.

NBPT.note: case L refused for 2014 and 2015

holding: He did not show exclusive or principal charge of his children for five years while living alone.
quote: divorcé depuis février 2005, puisse être regardé comme ayant supporté à titre exclusif ou principal la charge de ses enfants
notes: Joined with 2100805 (same judgment).

question: Whether the taxpayer qualifies for case L (raised a child alone for five years).
facts: Taxpayer without children at charge, claiming to have raised a minor child alone for more than five years.
assumptions: situation (single/divorced/widowed) not stated; any gives 1 part
no dependants

NBPT.note: case L removed for 2014 and 2015, appeal rejected

holding: Not shown that he had a child at his sole charge for five years; no case L.
quote: Le requérant n'est dès lors pas fondé à prétendre au bénéfice de la demi-part

question: Whether a widower qualifies for case L on the basis of a period of professional separation from his wife in 1968-1973.
facts: Widower; declared no child at charge in the five years after becoming a widower; says he looked after his child while living apart from his wife for work in 1968-1973.

NBPT.note: case L refused

holding: A separation for professional reasons is not living alone; case L refused. Alimony to a granddaughter also refused.
quote: n'a pas déclaré d'enfant à charge pendant les cinq années qui ont suivi son veuvage
notes: Same taxpayer and reasoning for 2017-2018 in TA Clermont-Ferrand 2101651 (marked duplicate).

question: Whether a divorced mother of four adult children qualifies for case L.
facts: Divorced in 2008; four children born 1979, 1982, 1985 and 1991, none at charge in the years in issue.

NBPT.note: case L refused for 2016 and 2017

holding: Not shown that she raised a child alone for five years while living alone.
quote: elle n'est pas fondée à soutenir que c'est à tort que l'administration fiscale a refusé de lui accorder une demi-part supplémentaire

question: Whether a woman divorced in 1988 qualifies for case L.
facts: Divorced on 16 Nov 1988; three children born 1965, 1968 and 1971; taxed as declared without case L for 2017-2019.

NBPT.note: case L refused, appeal rejected by order

holding: Not shown that she had sole charge of a minor child for five years while living alone.
quote: qui a divorcé de son mari le 16 novembre 1988, soutient avoir vécu seule avec ses trois enfants
notes: Appeal from TA Orléans 2101366 (marked duplicate).

question: Whether four years of sole charge of a child (2008-2011) satisfy case L.
facts: Woman separated in 2008, declared as parent isolé with her daughter (born 1993) for 2008-2011; the daughter filed her own return for 2012.
assumptions: situation single or divorced not stated; 0AD used

NBPT.note: case L refused: one year short

holding: Only four years of sole charge while living alone; case L refused.
quote: au cours des années 2008 à 2011, a déclaré ses revenus en tant que parent isolé et bénéficié de deux parts de quotient familial
notes: Years 2017-2019; 2019 used. Counts the five-year period in tax years of sole charge.

question: Whether a divorced man qualifies for case L.
facts: Divorced man who had previously (2006-2009) received a half-part as divorced living alone without children; no evidence he had his minor children at charge while separated.

NBPT.note: case L removed, appeal rejected by order

holding: Sole charge of a child for five years not shown; case L refused.
quote: il avait bénéficié d'une demi part supplémentaire en qualité de divorcé vivant seul sans enfant à charge

question: Whether a widow over 74 whose veteran husband died in 2012 before reaching 74 gets the half-part of art. 195, 1 f.
facts: Widow aged over 74; her husband, holder of the veteran card and pension, died in 2012 before the age of 74.
assumptions: declarant over 74 in 2019 (born before 1945); birth year not stated

NBPT.note: half-part refused for 2019

holding: The husband died before 74, the age required by art. 195, 1 f; the widow is not entitled.
quote: son époux est décédé avant d'avoir atteint l'âge de 74 ans, âge requis pour bénéficier des dispositions du f du I de l'article 195
notes: Compare TA Nantes 2103500, which states the opposite condition on the husband's age at death.

question: Whether a widow over 75 of an Algerian-war veteran gets the half-part of art. 195, 1 f.
facts: Widow over 75; her husband never received the half-part during his lifetime.
assumptions: declarant over 75 (born before 1941); birth year not stated

NBPT.note: half-part refused for 2014-2016

holding: The husband never had the half-part during his life; the widow is not entitled. Partial relief on a property-income deduction.
quote: dès lors qu'il n'a jamais bénéficié de la demi-part supplémentaire de quotient familial de son vivant
notes: Unusual wording: the court says only widows over 75 whose husband died BEFORE 74 and had a veteran pension qualify; TA Besançon 2200884 requires the husband to have reached 74.

question: Whether the reassessed 2017 taxable income and tax (scale part plus quotient on pension arrears) were overstated.
facts: Single filer (no spouse or dependants mentioned). Salaries 22,972; pensions 39,279 taxed normally and 100,625 of pensions taxed under the quotient system; foncier deficit 4,471 and deductible CSG 165 deducted from global income; life-insurance income 5,004 (2DH) under the 7.5% flat levy, excluded from the base; Pinel reduction 3,903 not disputed; a flat-levy credit of 345 deducted.
assumptions: Situation single (0AC) inferred from the absence of any spouse or dependant; not stated
0XX holds the 100,625 of pension arrears taxed under art. 163-0 A; number of years not stated (4 reproduces the court's 32,072 to within 2 euros)
4BC used for the 4,471 foncier deficit imputed on global income
Pinel reduction entered as an amount of 3,903 (no 7Q* box detail stated)
345 flat-levy credit treated as a credit; its basis is not stated
reviewer: only the 10 % deduction on the salary (between floor and cap, hence year-independent) is scored, on proxy years
holding: Administration upheld: taxable income 54,265 plus 97,925 under the quotient; tax 38,397, supplement 5,900 justified.
quote: c'est à bon droit que l'administration fiscale a retenu un revenu imposable de 54 265 euros et un revenu soumis au quotient de 97 925 euros
notes: 2017 scale and the 3,752 pension cap are year-dependent; ABAT10 (10% of 22,972 within the floor and cap) is year-independent. Check: scale tax on 54,265 for one part with the 2017 scale = 10,573; quotient with divisor 4 gives 32,074 vs 32,072 stated. Pension allowance cap allocated pro rata between quotient and ordinary pensions.

figure.note: ¶5: 10% pension allowance capped at 3,752, split 2,699 to quotient pensions and 1,053 to ordinary pensions (pro rata)
¶5: revenu imposable 54,265 plus revenu soumis au quotient 97,925
¶5: tax on income under the scale

question: Whether the 2018 foncier income (and hence taxable income and tax) was overstated.
facts: Single filer (no spouse or dependants mentioned). Salaries, pensions and annuities 66,697 after allowances (not disputed; gross amounts not stated). Foncier: own rental 425 plus share of SCI profit 2,154, less prior deficit 502 = 2,077. Pinel reduction 3,903 not disputed.
assumptions: Situation single (0AC) inferred; not stated
Salaries/pensions known only as 66,697 net of allowances; enter as net (gross and split not stated)
4BA = 425 + 2,154; 4BD = prior foncier deficit 502
Pinel reduction entered as an amount of 3,903
reviewer: taxable income 68 774 entered as net income in 4BA; only RNI -> IDRS is scored
holding: Administration upheld: taxable income 68,774, tax 14,834 before the Pinel reduction; supplement 3,752 justified.
quote: Le revenu imposable [...] étant ainsi de 68 774 euros, l'impôt relatif aux revenus soumis au barème s'élève ainsi à hauteur de 14 834 euros
notes: 14,834 matches the 2018 scale for one part on 68,774. Gross incomes not stated, so only RNI->IDRS is reproducible. CIMR not computed by the programs.

ITRED.why: Pinel reduction given as an amount; investment not stated

figure.note: ¶7: impôt net avant corrections 10,931 (then +2,425 advance clawback, -345 flat levy, -CIMR 14,834 = refund 1,823)
¶7: CIMR equal to the scale tax

question: Whether the 2019 foncier income (and hence taxable income and tax) was overstated.
facts: Single filer (no spouse or dependants mentioned). Salaries, pensions and annuities 78,363 after allowances (not disputed; gross not stated). Foncier 2,822 own rental plus 2,193 SCI share = 5,015. Deductible CSG 24. Pinel reduction 3,903 not disputed.
assumptions: Situation single (0AC) inferred; not stated
Salaries/pensions known only as 78,363 net of allowances; enter as net
Pinel reduction entered as an amount of 3,903
reviewer: taxable income 83 354 entered as net income in 4BA; only RNI -> IDRS is scored
holding: Administration upheld: taxable income 83,354, tax 20,122 before the Pinel reduction; supplements of 6,210 (with social levies) justified.

notes: 20,122 matches the 2019 scale for one part on 83,354.

ITRED.why: Pinel reduction given as an amount

question: Whether a 590,000 share gain on retirement, almost wholly relieved by the art. 150-0 D ter allowance, could still give rise to income tax and CEHR.
facts: Retiring company head sold shares on 9 December 2016 for a gain of 590,000, undeclared until a formal notice. Administration applied the fixed 500,000 allowance and then the 85% enhanced allowance on the 90,000 balance: taxable gain 13,500; income-tax supplement 5,536; CEHR 7,512 computed on an RFR including the allowances; household's other income and RFR not stated.
assumptions: Gross gain 590,000 = 3VG 13,500 + 3VA 500,000 (fixed allowance) + 3SL 76,500 (85% of 90,000)
Other household incomes and parts not stated
holding: Administration upheld (ordonnance): allowances do not reduce the CEHR base, which includes them under art. 1417 IV; IR supplement, CEHR and social levies confirmed.
quote: la plus-value brute imposable à l'impôt sur le revenu résultant de la cession des titres a été ramenée de 590 000 euros à 13 500 euros
notes: Same facts as TA Amiens 2022-07-07 n° 1902905 (duplicate). IR supplement 5,536 and CEHR 7,512 not reproducible (RFR/other income not stated); 7,512 = 3% x 250,400, i.e. consistent with a couple with RFR about 750,400, not with a single filer.

PV_NET.why: outside the programs: the holding-period/retirement allowances are computed on form 2074 and entered as amounts

question: Whether a taxpayer who filed late on paper could validly opt for the scale (with duration allowance) for a 2019 share gain, or the 12.8% flat rate applied.
facts: Taxpayer declared a 2019 gain of 1,513,301 on sale of shares, ticked the global option for the scale and deducted an 85% then 65% duration allowance; return filed on paper on 2 July 2020 after the 30 June deadline. Other incomes not stated.
assumptions: 1,513,301 taken as the gain before any duration allowance
No valid 2OP option (court); administration applied the scale with a 65% allowance
Other incomes and household not stated
holding: Taxpayer won: without an option made by the filing deadline the gain is taxed at the 12.8% flat rate; supplement reduced to the flat-rate tax.
quote: La plus-value d'un montant de 1 513 301 euros déclarée au titre de l'année 2019 est imposable au taux forfaitaire de l'article 200 A
notes: The PFU amount is derived from the holding, not stated. Unusual: the late return makes the flat rate more favourable than the scale with 65% allowance, so the late filing benefits the taxpayer.

figure.note: ¶4 and art. 1: gain of 1,513,301 taxed at the art. 200 A flat rate; 12.8% x 1,513,301 = 193,702.5 (amount not stated by the court)

PFU.why: not stated by the court (reader's computation from the holding)

question: Treatment of transaction payments disguised as dismissal indemnities; base of the 2016 reassessment.
facts: Taxpayer declared 81,864 of 2016 salaries, taxable 73,678 after the 10% deduction. Payments of 313,560 cashed in 2016 were taxed as distributed income (x1.25); the reassessed base was reduced by the 73,678 already taxed.
assumptions: Only the salary line is used; distributed income and household not modelled
holding: Administration largely upheld for 2016 (payments taxable as distributions, base reduced only by the 73,678 already taxed); 2017 base reduced by 50,844 already declared.
quote: a déclaré 81 864 euros de revenus au titre de l'année 2016 [...] soit un montant net imposable de 73 678 euros
notes: Only the 10% deduction is reproducible; it lies between the floor and the cap, so it does not depend on 2016 parameters.

question: How the PME subscription reduction is limited by the tax remaining and by the 10,000 overall ceiling of art. 200-0 A, and what can be carried forward.
facts: Couple (later divorced). After reassessment, tax before reductions 11,666. Reductions: accounting fees 719 (art. 199 quater B), Pinel-type reduction ('dispositif B') 5,500, PME subscription of 50,000 in 2017 (art. 199 terdecies-0 A). Incomes not stated.
assumptions: IDRS 11,666 must be taken as given: incomes are not stated
Married/joint filing assumed for 2017 (spouses called 'les époux')
'Dispositif B' is a pseudonymised name, taken to be the Pinel reduction (5,500)
PME subscription 50,000 in 2017
holding: Administration upheld for 2017: the unused part of the PME reduction limited by the tax due cannot be carried forward; only the 947 cut by the 10,000 ceiling is reportable.
quote: le montant de la réduction d'impôt pour investissement au capital d'une PME a été réduit de 947 euros
notes: The 10,000 overall ceiling is unchanged 2013-2019, so the ceiling cut is year-independent given IDRS; the 18% PME rate (9,000 on 50,000) never binds here because the remaining tax (5,447) is lower. Accounting-fee reduction treated by the court as outside the ceiling. IR_NET is derived.

figure.note: ¶9: PME reduction limited to the tax remaining 11,666-719-5,500, before the ceiling
¶9: 5,500 + 5,447 exceeds 10,000 by 947; PME reduction cut by 947
derived: 11,666 - 719 - 5,500 - (5,447 - 947) = 947; court states a 2017 supplement of 1,028

excluded: the gross tax is given, not the incomes; the reductions' bases are pseudonymised

question: Whether the 947 PME reduction cut by the 2017 ceiling is carried forward to 2018, and the consequent 1758 A surcharge.
facts: After reassessment, tax before reductions 9,983 (incomes not stated). Pinel-type reduction 5,500; carry-forward of the 947 PME reduction cut by the 2017 ceiling, conceded by the administration during the proceedings.
assumptions: IDRS 9,983 taken as given: incomes not stated
Household composition in 2018 not stated (divorce in progress)
holding: Partly for the taxpayer: the 947 carry-forward (already conceded) also reduces the 10% surcharge, discharged by 95; no further carry-forward allowed.
quote: pouvait également se prévaloir de la fraction de la réduction d'impôt pour investissement dans le capital des PME, qui avait été plafonnée en 2017
notes: Scorable only if the program accepts IDRS as given. Surcharge 95 = 10% x 947.

question: Acquisition price of shares received in an exchange (sursis) and resulting net gain on their 2017 sale.
facts: Shares received in a 2012 exchange for shares originally subscribed for 52,000 were sold on 11 December 2017 for 968,939. Administration taxed the net gain at 313,504 after imputing prior losses of 47,213 and a 65% duration allowance (stated as 569,010). Taxpayer claimed an acquisition value of 858,000 (gain 55,470). CEHR 2017 assessed; other incomes and RFR not stated.
assumptions: Gross gain taken as 968,939 - 52,000 = 916,939 (fees not stated)
Duration allowance 65% (shares held more than 8 years)
Taxpayer's version: price 968,939 - 858,000 = 110,939 before losses and allowance
holding: Administration upheld: acquisition price is the original 52,000 value of the shares contributed; net gain 313,504 maintained; CEHR maintained except a partial relief.
quote: le gain net constaté à l'occasion de cette cession qu'elle a évalué à 313 504 euros après imputation de moins-values antérieures d'un montant de 47 213 euros
notes: Court's figures look internally inconsistent: (968,939 - 52,000 - 47,213) x 35% = 304,404, not 313,504; and 569,010 is 65% of 875,400, while 313,504 + 569,010 = 882,514. Possibly fees or a different cost base not stated. Same facts as TA Dijon 2023-09-21 n° 2201053 (duplicate).

figure.note: ¶1 and ¶18: net gain 313,504 after losses 47,213 and 65% allowance of 569,010

question: Whether a non-resident's real-estate gain taxed by the art. 244 bis A levy enters the RFR on which the 2017 CEHR is assessed.
facts: Taxpayer resident in Switzerland sold a French property on 20 June 2017 with a net gain of 756,533 taxed by the art. 244 bis A levy, and declared it on her 2017 return. Administration assessed CEHR 17,761 on that basis. No other income mentioned.
assumptions: 3VZ used for the gain subject to the art. 244 bis A levy
Situation not stated; the administration's 17,761 equals the single-person CEHR schedule on 756,533
No other income assumed
holding: Taxpayer won: before the 2017 finance-law change, art. 244 bis A gains were outside the RFR, so no CEHR was due for 2017.
quote: le montant des plus-values soumises au prélèvement prévu à l'article 244 bis A n'était pas compris dans le revenu fiscal de référence du foyer fiscal
notes: Admin figure checks: 3% x (500,000-250,000) + 4% x (756,533-500,000) = 7,500 + 10,261 = 17,761 (single schedule). Rates unchanged since 2012, but the RFR definition changed: from 2018 income these gains enter the RFR, so a 2018/2019 program would return 17,761; the court's 0 holds only for 2017.

figure.note: ¶3 and art. 1: gains under art. 244 bis A were not part of the 2017 RFR (before the change made by loi 2017-1837)

CEHR.why: income 2017 rule (art. 244 bis A gains outside the RFR) changed for 2018: no program for 2017, a proxy year would apply a different law

question: Amount of the salary reassessment: difference of net-after-10% income (taxpayer) or of salaries actually received versus declared (administration).
facts: Taxpayer who opted for the standard 10% deduction; salaries actually received in 2018 found at 113 210 EUR (81 600 declared). Household composition not stated.
assumptions: Household/situation not stated; only the salary block is scorable.
113 210 is the taxable salary before the 10% deduction (the court calls it 'montant brut', but 113 210 x 0.9 = 101 889 as the court states).
No frais reels; standard 10% deduction applied (not capped: 11 321 < 2018 cap).
holding: The administration rightly reassessed 31 610 EUR (113 210 received - 81 600 declared); the taxpayer's claim that only 20 289 EUR (101 889 - 81 600) could be added is rejected.
quote: et, après cette vérification, à un montant de 101 889 euros
notes: Declared 81 600 -> 73 440 and found 113 210 -> 101 889 both equal exactly 90%, so the 10% deduction is uncapped in both versions.

figure.note: para 9: 'revenu net imposable' after verification; salaries net of the 10% deduction (other income of the household not described)

question: Whether prior furnished-letting (LMNP) deficits had to give a further reduction beyond their imputation on the 2018 LMNP profit of 9 891 EUR.
facts: Married couple. 2018 LMNP (BIC) profit 9 891 EUR fully offset by prior LMNP deficits (56 755 EUR available); after imputation taxable income 208 339 EUR instead of 218 230 EUR. Composition of the other income not stated.
assumptions: Number of dependants not stated (no children mentioned): 2 parts assumed.
Composition of income not stated; only RNI and the scale tax are given, so a program must be fed RNI directly.
CIMR and other credits are not reproducible from the facts given.
reviewer: taxable incomes entered as net income in 4BA; 2 parts (couple, no child mentioned) as the reader assumed

IDRS.note: para 3, 'impot sur les revenus soumis au bareme'

TAX_DELTA.note: reviewer: 61 647 on 218 230 (before the deficits) - 57 592 on 208 339 (after), both stated in the same sentence

holding: Request rejected: the deficits had already been imputed on the 2018 LMNP profit and the CIMR computed accordingly, so no further relief was due.
quote: soit un impôt sur les revenus soumis au barème de 57 592 euros au lieu de 61 647 euros
notes: Both pairs (208 339 -> 57 592; 218 230 -> 61 647) are consistent with the 2018 scale at 2 parts with no QF cap; parts were not stated by the court.

figure.note: para 3, income tax after CIMR and other credits (other credits not described)
para 3, after imputation of the LMNP deficits

question: Amount of 2015 donations within the 20% limit and the excess carried forward to 2016.
facts: Married couple; donations to general-interest bodies of 14 773 EUR in 2015; declared taxable income for 2015 of 64 575 EUR.
assumptions: The 64 575 EUR 'revenu imposable' is the base of the 20% limit as the court states; its composition is not given.
Donations are of the 66% regime (art. 200), not 75% aid bodies.
The dispute concerns the 2016 carry-forward; the computed figures are for 2015.

reviewer: the 'revenu imposable' 64 575 (base of the 20 % limit) entered as net income in 4BA; 66 % rate and 20 % limit unchanged 2015-2025, so run on proxy years; the retained base and the carry-forward are M variables (BON, REPDON); Lean outputs only the reduction imputed, which the tax caps here

DONS_BASE.note: para 4: donations within the limit for 2015

holding: The taxpayers do not show a calculation error; the 2015 excess carried forward is 1 397 EUR, not 3 479 EUR.
quote: les dons aux œuvres ouvrant droit à réduction d'impôt au titre de l'année 2015 l'étaient dans la limite de 13 376 euros
notes: Inconsistent with the statute on the stated facts: 20% x 64 575 = 12 915 (carry 1 858), whereas 13 376 = 20% x 66 880. The 20% limit and 66% rate did not change 2015-2019.

question: Net micro-BNC and micro-BIC results for 2016 after reclassification of invoices produced in the proceedings.
facts: Individual with an engineering/consulting activity (BNC, receipts 35 358,38 EUR HT in 2016) and a separate building-works activity (BIC services, receipts 34 155,29 EUR); the administration applied micro-BNC and micro-BIC.
assumptions: Household not stated.
Building works treated as BIC services (50% allowance) as the administration and court did.
Micro regimes applied as held, although 2016 receipts exceed the 32 900 EUR thresholds of that year.

MICRO_ABAT.note: derived: sum of the two allowances (12 021,85 + 17 077,64)

holding: The taxpayer's claims are rejected; the administration could tax the two activities separately under micro-BIC and micro-BNC.
quote: et, après abattement de 34 % prévu par l’article 102 ter du code général des impôts, un montant de 23 336,53 euros
notes: Allowance rates (34%, 50%; minimum 305) are year-independent. Odd: both 2016 receipts exceed the 2016 micro thresholds (32 900) yet micro regimes were applied; total income retained for 2016 was 72 329 EUR including unexplained income.

question: Whether category and prior global deficits are imputed on the ordinary income (court) or on the exceptional income itself (administration) under the quotient system.
facts: Deceased taxpayer's 2017 income: capital income 467 EUR, deductible CSG 24 EUR, 2017 agricultural deficit 23 879 EUR, prior global deficit carried forward 15 265 EUR, exceptional income net of its own charges 272 004 EUR taxed under art. 163-0 A.
assumptions: 0XX = exceptional income taxed with quotient 4 (art. 163-0 A I).
Capital income 467 entered as 2TR (category not specified; taken as its taxable amount).
Agricultural deficit 23 879 imputable on global income (5HF), as the court held.
Prior global deficit 15 265 entered as 6FL (year of origin not stated).
Household/parts not stated; the scorable figures are bases, not the tax.
holding: Deficits are imputed on the ordinary global income, to which a quarter of the exceptional income is then added; the minister's appeal is rejected.
quote: le déficit global ordinaire s'établit à - 38 701 euros, à quoi il y a lieu d'ajouter le quart du revenu exceptionnel net
notes: Pure arithmetic of the quotient method, no year parameter. The tax itself (4 x scale(29 300) - 4 x scale(<=0)) needs the number of parts, not stated. Text applies art. 163-0 A as in force before LF 2022.
excluded: the court's figures are internal steps of the quotient method with no program output; the parts are not stated

question: Whether a 2019 capital gain was exceptional for the quotient system, compared after the holding-period allowance.
facts: Couple who realised in 2019 a gain on securities of 718 171 EUR, taxed under the scale with the 85% holding-period allowance; average net income of the three previous years 128 092 EUR.
assumptions: 85% reinforced allowance applies as the court states (para 3); holding period itself not stated; 3SL = 85% x 718 171 rounded.
Option for the scale (2OP) assumed since the allowance only applies under the scale.
Situation (married/PACS) not stated explicitly; other income not stated.
holding: The net gain (107 726) does not exceed the 3-year average (128 092), so it is not exceptional; quotient refused (and the doctrine on gross amount could not be invoked as the taxpayers had not applied it in their return).
quote: conduit à ramener le montant net imposable de cette plus-value à la somme de 107 726 euros
notes: The court attributes the 85% rate to art. 150-0 D 1 ter (it is 1 quater). 718 171 x 15% = 107 725,65.

figure.note: para 3: average net income of the 3 previous years (quotient test)

question: Taxable base of a 2015 contribution gain not eligible for deferral, after the reinforced holding-period allowance.
facts: Taxpayer who contributed shares against new shares and a cash balance in 2015; gain to be taxed found at 418 880 EUR, reinforced allowance of 65% (art. 150-0 D 1 quater) admitted by the minister for income tax and CEHR.
assumptions: 3VG holds the gain before allowance; the 65% reinforced allowance applies as held (para 8).
Household and other income not stated.
holding: Gain computed under common-law rules at 418 880 EUR, reduced by the 65% reinforced allowance to 146 605 EUR; taxes on that base reinstated.
quote: après application de l’abattement de 65 % à cette somme, le montant de la base imposable s’établit à 146 605 euros
notes: Inconsistent: 418 880 x 35% = 146 608, not 146 605. The operative part also cites 418 800 (art. 1) and 418 000 (art. 2) as the social-levy base, against 418 880 in para 8.

question: Whether gains on share sales were exceptional (quotient), comparing the gain after allowance with the 3-year average income.
facts: Couple; gains on share sales/buy-backs of 231 300 EUR before allowance in 2015, holding-period allowance of 65% (art. 150-0 D 1 ter b); average taxable income 2012-2014 of 362 929 EUR.
assumptions: 65% allowance applies to all the 2015 gains (para 1); gains taxed under the scale (2OP).
Other income not stated.
holding: The gains after allowance do not exceed the 3-year average income; quotient refused, deliberate-failure penalty upheld.
quote: le montant de la plus-value, après abattement, en 2015 s'élève à 150 345 euros
notes: Inconsistent with the statute: 231 300 x (1 - 65%) = 80 955; 150 345 is exactly 65% of 231 300, i.e. the allowance itself (or the gain after a 35% allowance). The outcome is unaffected (both below 362 929).

figure.note: para 10: 'montant de la plus-value, apres abattement, en 2015'

question: Same as 2015: gain after allowance compared with the 3-year average income for the quotient system.
facts: Couple; gains on share sales/buy-backs of 1 167 166 EUR before allowance in 2017, holding-period allowance of 65% (art. 150-0 D 1 ter b); average taxable income 2014-2016 of 544 407 EUR.
assumptions: 65% allowance applies to all the 2017 gains (para 1); gains taxed under the scale (2OP).
Other income not stated.
holding: Gains after allowance below the 3-year average; quotient refused.
quote: le montant des plus-values, après abattement, en 2017 s'élève à 420 656 euros
notes: 1 167 166 x 35% = 408 508, not 420 656; the court's figure would require part of the shares to carry only a 50% allowance, contrary to para 1. Treat as inconsistent or as mixed holding periods not described.

question: Number of parts of a taxpayer married abroad in 2019 whose spouse and new-born child live abroad.
facts: Taxpayer married in January 2019 in Egypt under the default separation-of-property regime, spouse resident in Egypt; child born November 2019 living with the mother in Egypt.
assumptions: Distinct taxation under art. 6-4-a (separated property, not under the same roof) coded as 0AD.
Child not his dependant (lives with and is deemed in the exclusive charge of the mother).
Income amounts not needed for the parts.

NBPT.note: para 6: claim of 1,5 additional part rejected

holding: Parts claim rejected (distinct taxation, child not in his charge); but the late-reassessed distributed income may be taxed under the scale on his option, so the tax is reduced on that ground.
quote: n’est pas fondé à demander la réduction de son imposition au motif qu’il devrait bénéficier de 1,5 part supplémentaire
notes: The 2018 year in the same judgment concerns only the option for the scale (no parts dispute).

question: Net furnished-letting income under micro-BIC (and hence the treaty tax credit) for UK rents.
facts: Resident taxpayer letting a furnished property in the United Kingdom as a non-professional; gross rents 12 872 EUR in 2019; no option for the real regime.
assumptions: Non-professional furnished letting under micro-BIC (50% allowance), as held.
Household and other income not stated; the treaty credit (art. 24 France-UK) cannot be reproduced.
holding: Net income is 6 436 EUR after the 50% micro-BIC allowance; the treaty credit correspondingly halved to 626 EUR and offset against the social-levy refund; claim rejected.
quote: le revenu net locatif pour l'année 2019 de la contribuable s'établissait à 6 436 euros et non à 12 872 euros
notes: The court cites a 72 600 EUR micro-BIC threshold, which is the post-2020 figure (70 000 for 2019 for this category); no effect on the outcome.

figure.note: para 4: treaty credit reduced from 1 252 to 626; not reproducible from facts

question: Requalification of a bank credit from unexplained income to furnished-letting income under micro-BIC.
facts: Taxpayer whose 2017 bank credit of 7 403,22 EUR came from a non-professional furnished letting, of which 1 700 EUR was a security deposit; rents 5 703,22 EUR.
assumptions: Micro-BIC 50% allowance (minimum 305) applies as held; household and other income not stated.
holding: The 7 403,22 EUR taxed as unexplained income is replaced by BIC of 2 851 EUR (5 703,22 rents less 50% allowance; 1 700 deposit excluded); taxpayer partly discharged.
quote: ceux-ci sont imposables en tant que bénéfices industriels et commerciaux à hauteur de 2 851 euros compte tenu de l'abattement de 50 %
notes: Court truncates 2 851,61 to 2 851.
